\label{lemma-godement-resolution}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. For every sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ there is a resolution
$$
0 \to
\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to \ldots
$$
functorial in $\mathcal{F}$ such that each term
$f_*f^* \ldots f_*f^*\mathcal{F}$ is a flasque
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module and such that for all $x \in X$ the
map
$$
\mathcal{F}_x[0] \to \Big(
(f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to
(f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to
(f_*f^*f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to \ldots
\Big)
$$
is a homotopy equivalence in the category of complexes
of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules.
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $X_{disc}$ the same set with discrete topology. Let $f:(X_{disc},f^{-1}\mathcal O_X)\to(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be the canonical flat morphism of ringed spaces. Every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ has a functorial Godement resolution $0\to\mathcal F\to f_*f^*\mathcal F\to f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal F\to\cdots$ with flasque terms, and on each stalk $x\in X$ the augmented resolution is a homotopy equivalence of complexes of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules.
conclusions:
For every sheaf of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ there is a resolution
$$
0 \to
\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to
f_*f^*f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F} \to \ldots
$$
functorial in $\mathcal{F}$ such that each term
$f_*f^* \ldots f_*f^*\mathcal{F}$ is a flasque
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module and such that for all $x \in X$ the
map
$$
\mathcal{F}_x[0] \to \Big(
(f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to
(f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to
(f_*f^*f_*f^*f_*f^*\mathcal{F})_x \to \ldots
\Big)
$$
is a homotopy equivalence in the category of complexes
of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules.
semantic_review_note: On any ringed space, let f from the underlying discrete-point ringed space to X be canonical. The iterated f_*f^* construction yields a functorial flasque Godement resolution of every O_X-module with stalkwise HOMOTOPY equivalence, stronger than a quasi-isomorphism. The final statement supplies the missing definition of f and preserves the whole resolution and stalk property.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-godement-resolution-bounded-below}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let
$\mathcal{F}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. There exists a quasi-isomorphism
$\mathcal{F}^\bullet \to \mathcal{G}^\bullet$
where $\mathcal{G}^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of flasque
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules and for all $x \in X$ the
map $\mathcal{F}^\bullet_x \to \mathcal{G}^\bullet_x$
is a homotopy equivalence in the category of complexes
of $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$-modules.

semantic_review_note: Every bounded-below O_X-module complex admits a bounded-below complex of flasque sheaves quasi-isomorphic to it, with each stalk map a homotopy equivalence. The final preserves bounded-below on both source and target and stalkwise strength.
